snp2.8:1.2: —as the devas, Indra—one from whom you might learn the Dhamma,
snp2.8:1.4: confident in you, shows you the Dhamma.
snp2.8:2.2: practicing the Dhamma in line with the Dhamma,
snp2.8:2.4: heedful, befriending a teacher like that.
snp2.8:3.1: But if you consort with a piddling fool
snp2.8:3.2: who hasn’t come to the goal, and is envious,
snp2.8:3.3: without having cleared up the Dhamma right here,
snp2.8:3.4: you’ll go to death with your doubts unresolved.
snp2.8:4.1: Like a man gone down to a river—
snp2.8:4.3: and swept away in the current:
snp2.8:4.4: How can he help others across?
snp2.8:5.1: Even so: he who hasn’t cleared up the Dhamma,
snp2.8:5.2: attended to the meaning of what the learned say,
snp2.8:5.3: himself not knowing, his doubts uncrossed:
snp2.8:5.4: How can he get others to comprehend?
snp2.8:6.1: But as one who’s embarked on a sturdy boat,
snp2.8:6.3: would carry many others across there,
snp2.8:6.4: knowing the needed techniques, skillful, thoughtful.
snp2.8:7.3: can, knowing, get other people to comprehend—
snp2.8:7.4: when the conditions have arisen for them to lend ear.
snp2.8:8.1: So: you should befriend a person of integrity—
snp2.8:8.3: Practicing so as to know the goal,
snp2.8:8.4: having experienced the Dhamma, you get bliss.
